Explore the functional annotations from an MGnify assembly analysis. You will
find the KEGG orthologues (KOs) detected in the analysis, compare KEGG module
completeness, and inspect the KOs that make up an individual module.

Start with the example study [MGYS00006180](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/metagenomics/studies/MGYS00006180/overview),
or replace it with a study accession of your choice. Run the cells in order.

## Choose an analysis

Change `STUDY` to another study with assembly analyses. The first page of
analyses is loaded below; change `page=1` to retrieve another page.

```{webr}
library(jsonlite)

API <- "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/metagenomics/api/v2"
STUDY <- "MGYS00006180"

get_json <- function(path) {
  file <- tempfile()
  on.exit(unlink(file))
  download.file(paste0(API, "/", path), file, quiet = TRUE)
  fromJSON(file)
}

batch <- get_json(paste0("studies/", STUDY, "/analyses/?page=1&page_size=1000"))
analyses <- as.data.frame(batch$items)
if (!nrow(analyses)) stop("This study has no analyses.")
analyses <- analyses[analyses$pipeline_version == "V5", ]
if (!nrow(analyses)) stop("No v5 analyses on this page. Choose another study or page.")
head(analyses[c("accession", "experiment_type", "pipeline_version")])
```

## Read the result tables

The first analysis is selected automatically. Replace `ANALYSIS` with an
accession from the table to explore a different analysis. The analysis record
provides the KO counts and module-completeness tables.

```{webr}
ANALYSIS <- analyses$accession[1]
analysis <- get_json(paste0("analyses/", ANALYSIS))
downloads <- as.data.frame(analysis$downloads)

read_result <- function(description, ...) {
  urls <- downloads$url[downloads$short_description == description & downloads$file_type == "csv"]
  if (!length(urls)) stop(paste("No result file:", description, "— choose another analysis."))
  file <- tempfile()
  on.exit(unlink(file))
  download.file(urls[1], file, quiet = TRUE)
  read.csv(file, ...)
}

ko <- read_result("KEGG orthologues annotation", header = FALSE,
                  col.names = c("count", "accession", "description"))
modules <- read_result("KEGG pathway annotation")
cat(ANALYSIS, "—", nrow(ko), "KOs and", nrow(modules), "modules\n")
head(ko)
```

## Explore module completeness

A KEGG module describes a functional unit within a pathway. The completeness
value is the percentage of that module's functions found in the analysis. It
does not show whether an entire pathway is complete or active.

```{webr}
modules <- modules[order(modules$completeness, decreasing = TRUE), ]
cat(sum(modules$completeness == 100), "modules reported as complete\n")
head(modules[c("module_accession", "pathway_name", "completeness")], 10)
```

Plot the 15 highest-scoring incomplete modules. Change `15` to show more or fewer.

```{webr}
incomplete <- modules[modules$completeness < 100, ]
shown <- head(incomplete, 15)
if (nrow(shown)) {
  barplot(rev(shown$completeness), names.arg = rev(shown$module_accession),
          horiz = TRUE, las = 1, xlim = c(0, 100), col = "#007c80",
          xlab = "Module completeness (%)", main = "Incomplete modules")
} else {
  cat("No incomplete modules in this result table.")
}
```

## Inspect a module

Start with glycolysis (`M00001`), or choose an identifier from the tables above.
The table shows which KOs in the module were found and which were not found in
the analysis. A missing annotation does not necessarily mean that a function is
absent from the community.

```{webr}
#| define: [module_url]
MODULE <- "M00001"
selected <- modules[modules$module_accession == MODULE, ]
if (!nrow(selected)) stop("Module not found. Choose an identifier from the table.")
cat(selected$pathway_name, "—", selected$completeness, "% complete\n")

matching <- strsplit(selected$matching_ko, ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
missing <- strsplit(selected$missing_ko, ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
module_kos <- data.frame(
  accession = c(matching, missing),
  status = c(rep("Matching", length(matching)), rep("Missing", length(missing)))
)
module_url <- paste0("https://www.kegg.jp/module/", MODULE)
module_kos
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
html`<a href=${module_url} target="_blank" rel="noopener">View this module’s diagram on KEGG</a>`
```

The KEGG link opens the reference diagram for the selected module. It does not
colour the diagram with this analysis's results.

## View detected functions in KEGG Mapper

Download the detected KO identifiers below, then:

1. Open [KEGG Mapper Search](https://www.kegg.jp/kegg/mapper/search.html).
2. Under **Search mode**, select the **Reference** radio button. The default
   **hsa** mode expects human gene identifiers and gives no matches for this file.
3. Use **Or upload file** to select the downloaded `-KOs.txt` file, then click **Exec**.
4. Open a result such as **Glycolysis / Gluconeogenesis** to see the detected KOs
   highlighted on its pathway map.

The search highlights pathways containing functions detected in your analysis.
A pathway match does not mean that the entire pathway is complete.

```{webr}
#| define: [ko_text, ko_filename]
ko_text <- paste(unique(ko$accession[ko$count > 0]), collapse = "\n")
ko_filename <- paste0(ANALYSIS, "-KOs.txt")
cat(length(unique(ko$accession[ko$count > 0])), "detected KO identifiers ready to download")
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
DOM.download(new Blob([ko_text], {type: "text/plain;charset=utf-8"}), ko_filename, "Download KO identifiers")
```

## Running this code in your own environment

Install jsonlite from your R console:

```r
install.packages("jsonlite")
```

Run the R cells in RStudio or an R script. To save the KO identifiers locally,
use `writeLines(ko_text, ko_filename)`.

### Querying KEGG from RStudio

When working in a local R installation, the Bioconductor
[`KEGGREST`](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/KEGGREST.html)
package can be used to query KEGG directly. For example, this retrieves the
definition of a KEGG module:

```r
# Run locally in RStudio; this is not executed in the browser page.
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("KEGGREST")

library(KEGGREST)
keggGet("M00001")
```
